alignments.note: Suffix of the possessive preposition takes the English subject pronoun of the recast possessive clause (rules 40 and 43).
Verbless possessive clause with no `הָיָה` and no existential particle: the preposition is what makes it possessive and carries the *have* (rule 43).
Possessed noun keeps its own word.
Conjunction rendered *but*, which rule 14's open list covers.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17 and 24).

Corrected. The accepted alignment marked `אַף` `unrepresented` and gave the whole *Neither is there* to `אֵין`. But *Neither* carries the additive connection of `אַף` and the negation of `אֵין` together, with no English word spent on either morpheme in particular, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the two share one unit, exactly as rule 35 fuses a waw with a negative into *Nor*; the *is there* is the existential frame rule 50 hands to the whole unit, which rule 30 says does not defeat the condition. Rule 22's closing paragraph forbids marking `unrepresented` a morpheme whose sense the ASV has written inside a fused rendering, and rule 11 gives a function word first to the morpheme whose sense it carries. Headed on the negative under rules 23 and 35, and on *Neither* under rule 50, which heads the existential on the negation word and never on *there*. The competing readings are (a) the accepted one, and (b) giving a bare *Neither* to `אַף` and leaving `אֵין` only *is there*, which rule 50 excludes because all 28 corpus occurrences head the existential on its negation word.

The positive existential standing under the negative takes the quantifying *any* the ASV writes for it; a present morpheme takes its English before a supplied-determiner reading does (rules 11 and 50). This is also what keeps it outside the fusion above: *any* is English the ASV spends on this morpheme in particular, which rule 30 says defeats the one-rendering condition. The competing reading leaves *any* to `רוּחַ` under rule 15 and marks this particle `unrepresented`.
Construct noun keeps its own word.

review_notes: Corrected: `אַף` and `אֵין` now share one unit for *Neither is there*, headed on the negative. The accepted alignment left a present additive particle `unrepresented` beside the very English word that carries its sense, which rules 22 and 30 forbid; rule 2's preference for the smallest unit does not license that split, because the split is not clearly preferable to the fusion.

The doubled existential `אֵין־יֶשׁ` remains the hard point of the verse: *Neither is there* goes to the negative fusion and *any* to the positive particle, with the alternatives named in both units' notes under rule 8.
All thirteen source ids and all fifteen target ids are partitioned exactly once in the corrected array.
